Subject: Future-state infra: air-gapped site & renewal questions

Hi Priya,

As we approach our June renewal, we wanted to surface a change in scope that will affect both capacity and terms. We are finalizing a contract amendment request to add a fully air-gapped environment at our New London data center (customer-managed SAN + isolated network). High level asks:

- Dedicated clusters for the air-gapped site (prod + staging), roughly equivalent to our current prod cluster (8 vGPU-equivalent nodes)
- No egress/connectivity from the environment to Redwood-hosted control plane (we understand there will be an on-prem control plane variant)
- Rollout to occur during the renewal window, ideally provisioned and validated before contract start

Can you share ballpark pricing delta (annual) for adding the air-gapped site + the bundled committed capacity increase? Also: is it possible to start provisioning pre-renewal under a letter-of-intent (LOI) since procurement timelines will push the PO close to the renewal date?

I've attached our initial network_requirements_medlytics.xlsx and included procurement on the thread. Laura (CISO) will join shortly with security questions.

Thanks,
Theo
Director of Platform Engineering
MedLytics Health

Hi Theo — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the network sheet. This is doable but there are a few moving parts (SOW/pricing, security evidence, and provisioning lead time). Proposed next steps:

1) Quick sync (30m) this week to align on topology and acceptance criteria (CC'ing Marcus for sizing + Grace for rollout sequencing).
2) We will produce a term amendment (SOW + pricing) that includes: dedicated clusters for air-gapped prod and staging, a committed capacity bump (baselined to current usage + 25%), and optional 3-year discounted term.
3) We can provision a staging air-gapped cluster ahead of the PO under an LOI with a refundable prepayment to cover initial capacity. Legal will want explicit rollback/failure clauses — my renewals lead (Neha) will draft the language.

Ballpark numbers (very high level until Marcus confirms): +$220k/year for the additional air-gapped cluster pair (support, ops, remote install), or +$180k/year if you take a 3-year commitment. Committed capacity increase (25%) roughly +$45k/year.

Can you share expected acceptance window and whether the New London site is reachable by our field-install team? If it's strictly air-gapped with no connectivity, we'll coordinate an on-site installer and customer-supplied jump host for control-plane ops.

I'll set up the call — options: Thu 2026-05-13 09:00 or Fri 2026-05-14 10:00 PT.

Theo / Priya — following up with technical sizing and delivery notes after a quick review of the network spreadsheet and our install playbook. Key points:

- Sizing: For parity with your current prod cluster we recommend two cluster groups: 1) Prod: 8 GPU nodes (NVIDIA A40 equivalent), 2) Staging: 3 GPU nodes. If you want headroom for batch/overnight, add +2 nodes to prod.
- Storage: Customer-managed SAN acceptable; we'll need iSCSI/NFS endpoints and performance baseline.
- Connectivity: If the site is fully air-gapped (no outbound), we provide an on-prem control-plane appliance that runs offline; it requires an initial bootstrap via a temporary bastion and periodic offline bundle updates.
- Timeline: Field install + validation: 4–6 weeks from signed LOI and prepayment for hardware access. Onboarding + 2 week soak in staging before cutover.

Cost drivers: on-site field engineer days (est. 8 days), offline control-plane license delta, and additional monitoring/retention for isolated logs. I've attached the installation_playbook.pdf with the checklist we'll use.

Next technical asks:
- Laura / security: confirm encryption expectations (KMS/HSM on-prem vs Redwood-managed), and acceptance tests for the offline control plane.
- Procurement: confirm whether a PO can reference an LOI and if a refund mechanism for the prepayment is required.

Attachment: installation_playbook.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Briggs <lbriggs@medlytics.com>

Hi Marcus / Priya,

Quick security checklist from my side before we proceed to SOW:
- Do you provide SOC 2 Type II report and a summary of penetration testing specific to the on-prem installer?
- For the offline control plane: is the control plane encrypted at rest using a customer-managed HSM (preferred)? If not, what mitigations are available?
- Can you describe the telemetry/logging flow and retention policy for an isolated cluster (we need assurance that logs never cross our external network boundary)?

Also: we'll require an on-site background check for any field engineers and an approval window for their access.

If you can provide the SOC2 report and a proposed HSM/crypto design, we can move to procurement.

Best,
Laura Briggs
CISO | MedLytics Health
